proposals: NSE and BSE should publish a quarterly statistic of listed stocks by price band, with count, median market cap, median traded value and share paying any dividend, so that the ₹0–50 band’s 2,086 stocks and their zero median dividend yield are visible from exchange data, not only from private screeners.

NSE and BSE should publish free, adjusted daily price histories for every listed security, including BSE-only scrips, so that independent analysis of the cheapest band is not limited to the 80–91% of priced stocks this post could compute a beta for, a minority of each band’s full count.

SEBI should require brokers’ order screens to show market capitalisation, average daily traded value and trailing dividend next to the price for stocks quoted under ₹50, so that a low price tag is not read as a proxy for value when the post finds it tracks small size and high beta instead.

SEBI should direct the exchanges to publish an annual report on retail participation by price band, showing unique investors and retail share of turnover, so that it is measurable how many savers sit in the segment with the worst Sharpe ratio (0.20) and median 1-year return (−22.7%) found here.
